title: The tent of meeting as the creators' residence
statement: Per the canon, the sanctuary dictated at Sinai — the canon cites Exodus 26 — was a residence the Israelites built to the creators' own plans for a team staying on Earth for a time: the tent of meeting, where the creators met the people's representatives and where food and goods were brought, read as provisioning and 'a pledge of submission'; Moses' face-to-face exchanges at the tent door (Exodus 33:9-11) are read as conversation with a suited creator; the corpus records the reading at the canon's level, with the mainstream account of the Tabernacle as a priestly sanctuary tradition in its own voice.

includes: The residence-to-plan reading as the canon states it: a residence fashioned by the Israelites 'suivant leurs plans', dictated in Exodus 26, and named the tent of meeting (TBWTT-3:36; Exodus 25:8-9, 26)

The provisioning reading of the offerings: fresh food and riches requested by a team residing for a time on Earth, and the Levitical approach rules read as provisioning discipline (TBWTT-3:34-35, 3:43-45; Exodus 25:2-7; Leviticus 21:17-18)

The face-to-face reading: Moses speaking with Yahweh at the tent door read as conversation with a creator protected by a suit, the atmosphere difference being the canon's stated reason (TBWTT-3:38-42; Exodus 33:9-11, 33:20)

The two contact modes as the canon distinguishes them: presence and direct exchange at the tent when the creators were near, the Ark's transmitter-receiver when they were distant (TBWTT-3:95-96) — this clause rides on woh-claim-0040 and does not restate the device reading
excludes: Adjudication of the two-tents problem: the canon merges the tent Moses pitched 'without the camp' (Exodus 33:7) with the priestly Mishkan at the camp's centre; the record registers that the canon merges them and does not settle the source-critical question
Architectural, dimensional, or material reconstruction of the structure beyond what the canon states

The cloud and the 'glory' filling the Tabernacle (Exodus 40:34-38) read as a craft; the canon makes the glory-as-craft reading at Sinai (TBWTT-3:32-33, Exodus 24:17), not at the Tabernacle, and extending it needs its own record

Any sequence of reception sites running from the Tabernacle through the Temples to the Embassy; the canon calls Solomon's Temple 'la première résidence pour l'accueil des Elohim' (TBWTT-3:102), the continuity question is unrecorded, and the Embassy identification is woh-claim-0016's alone
Historicity and dating of the wilderness period
The other furnishings: the Ark is woh-claim-0040, the Menorah woh-claim-0069, and the altars, table, and laver have no record
Jewish and Christian theologies of the Mishkan (the Shekhinah; the Epistle to the Hebrews' typology), preserved in their own voice

alternatives.statement: The Tabernacle of Exodus 25-31 and 35-40 is the priestly writer's Temple projected into the wilderness; no desert structure stands behind the specifications (the Wellhausen line).

Source criticism separates an oracle tent pitched outside the camp (Exodus 33:7-11; Numbers 11-12) from the priestly Mishkan at the camp's centre; the canon's reading depends on a harmonization the texts themselves resist.

'Food of God' and the gift language of sacrifice are ordinary ancient Near Eastern temple idiom expressing a theology of divine dwelling; nothing in them describes the provisioning of resident beings. (Haran; metadata only)
The residence-and-provisioning reading belongs to the 1970s ancient-astronaut register rather than arising from the texts, as alt-0040-speculation-lineage argues for the Ark.
